identity.title: ALMA Observations of Warm Molecular Gas and Cold Dust in NGC 34

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA Cycle-0 observations of the CO (6-5) line emission (rest-frame frequency = 691.473 GHz) and of the 435$\mu m$ dust continuum emission in the nuclear region of NGC 34

evidence.quote: a local luminous infrared galaxy (LIRG) at a distance of 84 Mpc ($\rm 1\ensuremath{''} = 407\; pc$)

question.value: How is warm dense molecular gas and cold dust distributed in the nucleus of NGC 34, how is it related to the starburst and AGN, and is there evidence for a molecular outflow?

evidence.quote: (1) How is the warm dense molecular gas distributed in the inner most region of NGC 34? (2) How is the gas related to the starburst and the AGN, respectively?
were carried out using the Band 9 receivers of ALMA in the TDM mode (velocity resolution: 6.8 km sec$^{-1}$)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 SPWs centered at 679.801, 678.039, 676.271, 674.339 GHz, each ~2 GHz wide

evidence.quote: are centered at the sky frequencies of 679.801, 678.039, 676.271 and 674.339 GHz, respectively, each with a bandwidth of $\sim 2$ GHz
CO (6-5) line emission (rest-frame frequency = 691.473 GHz)
$\rm H^{13}CN\; (8-7)$ line emission (rest-frame frequency = 690.552 GHz)
Observations were carried out in both extended (E) and extend & compact (E&C) configurations
having the FWHM of $\rm 0.26\ensuremath{''}\times 0.23\ensuremath{''}$ (corresponding to physical scales of $\rm 106\; pc \times 94\; pc$)

evidence.quote: channel maps of the CO (6-5) line emission have 1-$\sigma$ rms noise of $\rm 5.5\; mJy\; beam^{-1}$
The total on-target integration time was 2.25 hours.

findings_qualitative.value: CO(6-5) disk is regular, compact (200 pc FWHM) rotating, 6x smaller than the CO(1-0) disk; closely follows the radio continuum

evidence.quote: The CO (6-5) disk is a factor of 6 smaller than the CO (1-0) disk found by (cite: Fernandez2014).

claims.hypothesis: Warm dense gas in NGC 34 forms a compact regular rotating disk
claims.experiment: CO(6-5) imaging at 0.25'' with moment maps and P-V diagram
claims.result: Disk FWHM 200 pc, double-horn spectrum, FWHM 406 km/s

evidence.quote: consistent with a compact rotating disk with a size of 200 pc

claims.hypothesis: AGN contributes significantly to CO(6-5) and continuum
claims.experiment: Core flux fraction within r~50 pc
claims.result: Core is 19% of CO and 28% of continuum

evidence.quote: consistent with insignificant contributions of the AGN to both emissions

claims.hypothesis: Red wing feature is H13CN(8-7) or an outflow
claims.experiment: Flux ratio compared with NGC 4418 prediction and PDR models; outflow rate estimate
claims.result: Ratio 0.018±0.002 consistent with prediction; outflow rate 32 Msun/yr consistent with upper limit

evidence.quote: We cannot rule out either of the two scenarios

claims.hypothesis: Nuclear region has very high gas column density
claims.experiment: Gas and dust profiles from CO and continuum

evidence.quote: indicate a very high gas column density

why_this_data.value: NGC 34 chosen as one of the closest LIRGs with strong CO(6-5) and low zenith angle for Band 9

evidence.quote: its Band 9 observations are affected by minimal atmospheric absorption

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: H13CN line versus outflow explanation for the red wing; both retained

evidence.quote: the feature in the red-shifted wing of CO (6-5) profile can be due to the $\rm H^{13}CN$ line emission or/and an outflow

limitations_admitted.value: Good map quality only in the central ~3'' due to uv-coverage; astrometric accuracy ~0.1''

evidence.quote: the resulting maps have good quality only in the central region of $\sim 3''$ (limited by the uv-coverage)

referee_caveats_inferred: Gas mass differs by factor ~5 depending on alpha_CO; rests on CO(1-0) beam assumption
Single dust temperature from a formalism, not fit
Feature at red wing ambiguous; no independent line
Flux uncertainty 15% dominates; no systematic uv-coverage test
